evals.prompt: This method succeeds, returns a failure value when the downstream call is rejected, and throws when the input is out of range. Only the success case is covered.
evals.expected_output: One test per uncovered branch, and nothing beyond them.
expectations: Adds a test for the rejection path and a test for the out-of-range throw
Asserts the specific error raised, not merely that something was raised
Adds no second test for a branch that is already covered
Derives the list of cases from the implementation's branches rather than from the happy path

evals.prompt: Get this model to full coverage. It has a couple of plain accessors, a framework-declared relation, and one method with a rule in it.
evals.expected_output: A test for the method that carries logic, with a reason given for skipping the rest.
expectations: Tests only the member that carries logic
Does not test plain accessors or that the framework's own relation works
Says why the rest is not worth covering rather than silently omitting it
Does not treat a coverage percentage as the goal

evals.prompt: Cover this rate lookup for each of its four tiers.
evals.expected_output: One parameterized case listing the four tiers.
expectations: Uses the language's data provider or table-case mechanism rather than four near-identical tests
Keeps one row per tier with its expected result
Names the case after the behaviour rather than after the method under test
Does not repeat the arrange and assert for each tier

evals.prompt: The existing test asserts that a collaborator's method was called once. Make it prove something.
evals.expected_output: An assertion on the observable outcome, replacing the call-count assertion.
expectations: Asserts on state or a return value a caller depends on
Does not assert on internal call counts or private state
Uses a fake or the real collaborator rather than an expectation-heavy mock
Points out that the old assertion would survive a broken implementation

evals.prompt: Test that the totals calculation adds up correctly across its line items.
evals.expected_output: A test built from real value objects, with nothing mocked.
expectations: Constructs the real value objects rather than mocking them
Mocks nothing, because nothing here crosses an external boundary
Keeps the arrange to what the assertion needs
Asserts the result rather than the intermediate calls

evals.prompt: This suite has one consistent style, a shared base case, and its own factory helpers. Add coverage for the new flow.
evals.expected_output: Tests in the suite's existing style, using its existing helpers.
expectations: Matches the style of the existing test files rather than introducing a second one
Uses the suite's existing helpers instead of new bespoke setup
Copies the shape of the nearest existing test for a comparable change
Introduces a new mechanism only after saying why the existing shape cannot express the change

evals.prompt: Add a retry with backoff to the dispatcher, and test it.
evals.expected_output: Implementation and tests together, with write-code governing the implementation.
expectations: Loads write-code for the production change rather than writing it from this skill alone
Covers the retry path, the give-up path, and success on the first attempt
Controls the clock rather than waiting in real time
Keeps the tests in the shape the existing suite uses

evals.prompt: This test configures a stub to return a value, then asserts it got that value back. Make it worth something.
evals.expected_output: A test that would fail if the code under test did nothing.
expectations: Replaces the assertion with one about what the code actually did
Identifies that the original assertion validates the stub setup rather than application behaviour
Does not keep the tautological assertion alongside the new one

evals.prompt: I added a one-line guard for a missing value. Does that need tests?
evals.expected_output: One regression test for the missing-value case, and a clear no to anything more.
expectations: Recommends a single test for the missing value
Does not propose a suite of cases around a one-line guard
Says plainly where the existing suite already covers the present-value path
Does not create a new test file where an existing one covers the same component

evals.prompt: This test fails in CI but passes locally, and it is blocking the build. Get it green.
evals.expected_output: The test fixed, or skipped with a stated reason. Never deleted or commented out.
expectations: Does not delete the test or comment it out
Marks it skipped with the reason and what would resolve it, if it is not fixed outright
Offers the real fix, such as removing the environmental dependency, as the preferred option
Leaves the test discoverable in the suite rather than hidden in a comment

evals.prompt: Add cases for the normal result, an alternate result, two boundary inputs that hit the same branch, and an exception.
evals.expected_output: Cases ordered from success through alternatives and boundaries to failure, with duplicate branch coverage removed.
expectations: Orders cases from the primary success path through alternatives and boundaries to the exception
Follows a different repository-enforced ordering where one exists
Keeps only one of the two boundary inputs when both exercise the same behavior
Asserts the specific exception and observable outcomes

evals.prompt: Write Go tests for three invoice tiers with identical setup and assertion, plus a storage failure that needs different setup and assertions.
evals.expected_output: One table test for the tiers and a separate focused storage-failure test.
expectations: Uses named table rows for the three equivalent tier cases
Keeps the shared arrange, act, and assert in one table body
Tests the storage failure separately because its setup and assertion differ
Reports got before want in useful failure messages

evals.prompt: Test that a Go processor finishes asynchronous work before a context deadline.
evals.expected_output: Explicit completion synchronization selected against context cancellation, without time.Sleep.
expectations: Waits on an observable completion or error channel
Selects against context cancellation or a controlled deadline
Does not use time.Sleep to guess when work finished
Leaves no goroutine whose completion the test does not own
